title: kv-cache: compacting allocator and spillover paging to reduce fragmentation and eviction churn
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: Long-running chat workloads and multi-model routing increased KV cache fragmentation and eviction churn, causing higher p99 latencies and more frequent backend fetches. This PR introduces a compacting allocator for the in-GPU KV cache, a lightweight page abstraction to group adjacent KV segments, and a spillover/paging path that moves cold pages to host memory (and optionally SSD) before evicting them permanently. The goal is to reduce fragmentation, smooth eviction behavior across sequence-length distributions, and provide deterministic memory bounds for Dedicated/private runtimes. Changes include a new page table, on-GPU compaction pass triggered at configurable thresholds, an async spillover worker with backpressure-aware IO, and metrics and knobs for tuning eviction aggressiveness. Rollout: feature-flagged, staged canary in perf-canary followed by gradual percentage rollout across Dedicated pools. Key results from perf canary: 12% p99 token latency reduction, 18% throughput uplift for mixed short/long conversation traces, and up to 32% reduction in peak GPU KV memory for long-context tests.

review_comments:
Marco Chen: Can we guarantee compaction pause times under 2ms for 32K token caches? Suggest adding incremental compaction to avoid SLO spikes.
Priya Kapoor: Added an incremental compaction pass that runs between batches; benchmarked at ~0.9ms avg impact in the canary, details in perf results.

Jamal Ortiz: Spillover IO on overloaded nodes could cause backpressure into scheduler; how do we avoid cascading slowdowns?
Priya Kapoor: Spillover worker uses an async token-bucket and will throttle itself and expose kv.page_backpressure metric; also added a fallback to drop oldest pages when IO is saturated.

Erin Liu: Tests look good, but need more rigid error handling on allocation failures and clear observability for partial compaction runs.
Priya Kapoor: Added explicit allocation failure counters and per-run compaction status metrics; updated tests to assert on metrics as well.
Marco Chen (LGTM after changes): Approving; please ensure canary run for Dedicated pools before broad rollout.
ci_checks: perf-smoke: initial-fail (regression detected in stress transient), rerun: pass
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: compaction to reduce fragmentation, page-based spillover to host memory to avoid costly evictions, new metrics and config knobs. Expected impact: reduced p99 latency and lower peak GPU memory on long context workloads.
test_summary: Unit coverage added for allocator and spillover worker; perf canary run across mixed traces (short/long context) with 10k+ requests showed 12% p99 improvement and stable SLOs. No regressions in integration tests.
backout_plan: Feature-gated behind kv.compaction.enabled; quick rollback by disabling flag and draining spillover workers. If rollback required, revert the merge and redeploy runtime binaries following hotfix playbook.
notes_for_ops: Operators should tune kv.compaction.threshold and kv.spillover.host_threshold based on Dedicated pool memory footprints. Monitor kv.page_spill_count, kv.page_backpressure, and kv.compaction_runs before expanding rollout.
